correctness.rationale: Axis strictness and compactness imply the transverse clearance functions \(\rho_1(\delta),\rho_2(\delta)\to0\). Choosing two coordinate slices and applying \(\mathrm{SSD}(d)\mathrm P\) with \(s=d/2>0\) forces \(s\|v\|\le\rho_1(\delta)\) from the first slice and \(s\|u\|\le\rho_2(\delta)\) from the second. For sufficiently small \(\delta\), monotonicity of the absolute norm gives \(\|(u,v)\|<1/2\), contradicting the required common direction of norm greater than \(1/2\). Regrouping coordinates proves the arbitrary \(\ell_p\)-sum corollary. No finite experiment is used.
risks: The proof requires \(d>0\) and does not cover axis-flat norms such as \(\ell_\infty\).

originality.rationale: The primary 2018 direct-sum theorem was inspected in full at its relevant theorem: it excludes non-\(\ell_\infty\) absolute sums only at the endpoint \(\mathrm{SSD}2\mathrm P\). The 2020 quantitative paper was inspected at the definition and direct-sum propositions: it defines \(\mathrm{SSD}(d)\mathrm P\) and gives the one-way implication from quantitative almost squareness, but does not convert endpoint failure or failure of \(s\)-ASQ into failure at every positive \(d\). The audited two-slice clearance argument supplies that missing quantitative obstruction for the axis-strict class. Resultary searches found no implication-equivalent prior theorem.

value.rationale: The result closes a genuine quantitative gap left by the endpoint direct-sum theorem: for a natural geometric class of absolute norms, including every finite \(\ell_p\) norm, the entire positive symmetric strong diameter scale collapses independently of the summand spaces. This sharp qualitative-to-quantitative boundary is structurally useful and not a routine reformulation.

limitations: Axis strictness is sufficient, not claimed necessary.
No claim for \(d=0\), \(\ell_\infty\), or nonsymmetric diameter properties.
